With all of the stuff in your post and no specific questions (like "What does this word mean?" or "Why doesn't this thing work?"), it comes across as you asking people to explain how to do a bunch of mechanics for your game, which probably no one will do.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Yes, there is no way to change the UI from the editor (aside from the check boxes to show/hide specific menu items).
If you look in the options in the System 2 tab, you can simply turn off the Skill and Formation commands. To change what's shown in the actor's info, you'll need a plugin.

Considering the amount of incredibly basic things you have had to ask for help, I think that:
Delta44 said:
I wanted to make a top-down shooter
Click to expand...
Which involves:
Delta44 said:
edit the UI since this is not really an RPG style game
Click to expand...
This is all a very bad idea.
The tool is called RPG Maker for a reason, and not Doom-clone Maker.
You are trying to stretch the engine beyond what it is designed to do. Can it do it? Yes. But is it recommended? No, not really, especially, especially not for someone who is a complete and utter beginner to the engine.
What I recommend you do is to take a step back.
Begin a new project that is small in scope. This should involve just using the basic database functions built into the engine. So basically that means you're making an RPG or a horror/walking sim game.
Learn how the engine functions, learn how switches and variables work in an event-based context, and better understand how the engine functions.
Startng with plugins, making the game function in a way that the engine was not built to accomodate, all while not understanding this software is a bad idea.
Shelve this idea, and come back later when you are more competent with your skills.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
Delta44 said:
why does that happen?
Click to expand...
if the game cant complete the movement route because a portion of it is blocked, but you tell the game that the route must be completed before continuing, it will do that.
in a cutscene, chances are that you know where all your events and the player will be, so giving them move routes where they dont get stuck shouldnt be an issue. if you need to give move routes to events and you dont know of the event's starting position, there are a few plugins that will allow you to tell an event to go to a specified coordinate instead of saying "left, left, up, etc."

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Yes, if an Event during a Cutscene can't complete the set Route, your game will be stuck, as they try to proceed. So, avoid that.
If you can't ensure a safe route for any reason, you can either select "Skip if cannot move", so the character will ignore moving orders if the destination is blocked. Or you set the Event on "Through", so they walk through every obstacle in their route.
If they stop moving without a visible obstacle, you might have a wrong passability set to your tilesets or there is an invisible event in the way with blocking passability settings.
In 99% of your cases it should be pretty easy to figure out what was blocking your way.
